# Davos: Musk's Take on AI, Robotics and Superintelligence
By [Rithula Nisha Ebrahim](https://aimagazine.com/author/rithula-nisha-ebrahim)
January 23, 2026
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/ce1f881571e125bf989254966f80b010:8ca65f1477210240dd3ad0017e368e0e/image001-1.webp)
Elon Musk believes that humanoid robots like Capgemini and Orano's Hoxo will soon be commonplace \| Credit: Capgemini Credit: Capgemini
Elon Musk’s surprise appearance at the WEF in Davos saw him predict that AI will surpass collective human intelligence and robots will outnumber people
Elon Musk made an unexpected appearance at the World Economic Forum in Davos, marking a notable reversal for the tech billionaire who has previously criticised the annual gathering as "elitist" and "unelected".
He framed his work across Tesla, SpaceX and xAI around a singular ambition: to "maximise the probability that civilisation has a great future". Central to this vision is the rapid advancement of AI and robotics, technologies he believes will [fundamentally reshape human society within the next decade](https://aimagazine.com/news/studying-musks-ai-utopia-where-money-disappears).
## AI could surpass human intelligence
Elon provided a striking prediction for the timeline of [artificial general intelligence](https://aimagazine.com/articles/how-agi-will-ultimately-reshape-everything), suggesting that AI may soon exceed human cognitive capabilities across all domains.
"I think we might have AI that is smarter than any human by the end of 2026," he says, adding that this milestone would likely occur "no later than next year".
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/694d7f09410fa551ed87811e22ecba41:3a96e5ec9046c655f818c7725f4d5ab7/elon-bbc.jpeg)
Tesla CEO Elon Musk
Looking further ahead, he predicted that, by "2030 or 2031, AI will be smarter than all of humanity collectively".
According to Elon, the progression represents a major shift in the context of civilisation. He suggested that the exponential growth of AI capabilities would eventually "saturate human needs" and trigger unprecedented economic expansion on a global scale.
This transformation could be powered by AI systems that exceed the combined intellectual capacity of every human on Earth.
## Robots outnumbering humans
Perhaps the most ambitious prediction from Elon's Davos appearance was his assertion that "there will be more robots than people" in the coming decades.
He argued that the convergence of advanced AI and robotics represents "the path to abundance for all," potentially offering solutions to global poverty and labour shortages.
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/18a95d3a636092cd77aeee59aeda12f5:03df3bc6d59f745bb77a66b2a1e7c1c5/7-tesla-optimus-robots.JPG)
Tesla's Optimus humanoid robots
"The only way to do this is AI and robotics," Elon told Larry during the interview.
He envisions a future where robots become "ubiquitous," driving "an explosion in the global economy" that could dwarf current industrial output.
This transition would fundamentally alter the nature of work, as "everyone on Earth" may eventually rely on [robotic assistance for both domestic and industrial tasks](https://aimagazine.com/news/siemens-ai-powered-humanoid-robots).
## Tesla's Optimus launching commercially
Tesla's humanoid robot, Optimus, could progress from factory prototype to consumer product by 2026, according to Elon's timeline.
He revealed that Optimus units are currently performing "simple tasks in the factory," with more sophisticated capabilities expected soon.
"By the end of this year, I think they will be doing more complex tasks and, probably by the end of 2026, I think we'd be selling humanoid robots to the public," he says.
![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/DrNcXgoFv20/hqdefault.jpg)
Elon expressed confidence that, by late 2026, the robots would achieve "very high reliability" and be capable of performing almost any task requested by a human owner. He highlighted potential applications in elder care for ageing populations, suggesting robots could provide essential support in societies facing demographic challenges.
He asked the audience: "Who wouldn't want a robot to, assuming it's very safe, watch over your kids, take care of your pets?"
He framed humanoid robots as domestic utilities that could become staples in households worldwide, fundamentally reducing the burden of manual labour and care work.
## Safety concerns remain critical
"We need to be very careful with robotics," he went on. "We don't want to find ourselves in a James Cameron movie. Love his movies, but we don't want to be in Terminator, obviously."
This emphasis on safety comes as his AI startup, xAI, faces scrutiny from international regulators over "sexually explicit content" generated by its Grok chatbot, leading to demands for tighter safeguards.
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/c5a8b110c0e64a450382b031a7344885:715ddb6d3731eb6bc17d45e7f1f7719a/gettyimages-2198965772.jpg)
Tesla's Elon Musk has seen his xAI Grok chatbot running into controversy over explicit images (Credit: Getty)
The billionaire's predictions paint a picture of a world transformed by intelligent machines within the next five years, fundamentally altering economics, labour and daily life.
When asked about his personal ambitions and his well-known goal of colonising Mars, Musk joked about his mortality on the Red Planet: "People ask me ‘do I want to die on Mars? and I'm like: 'yes, but not on impact'."

# Jensen Huang: The Leader Powering the Global AI Revolution
By [Tom Chapman](https://aimagazine.com/author/tom-chapman)
January 23, 2026
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/3ed955f827095e24e4288b40c5a1175a:e592637c88a68b57193e2aeed6d03765/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-oracle-ceo-safra-catz-oracle-openworld-2022-1.webp)
Jensen Huang, CEO at NVIDIA
Jensen Huang's position at No.2 on the Top 100 AI Leaders 2026 list places him among the pioneering figures shaping how AI is built, adopted and governed
Jensen Huang has become one of the defining leaders of the AI era, turning NVIDIA into the infrastructure layer that powers modern model training and deployment.
His position at No.2 on [AI Magazine](https://aimagazine.com/)’s list of the Top 100 Leaders 2026 places him among the pioneering figures shaping how AI is built, adopted and governed.
_**To read the Top 100 list in full, [click here](https://aimagazine.com/magazine/top-100-ai-leaders-2026).**_ 
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/49378dc8f9ce8583f092159c8cc32a01:069de6dc80c0c9c23a6f6d934785ba1d/gettyimages-2248009084.jpg)
NVIDIA is one of the world's most valuable companies. Picture: Getty Images
## Formative years
Jensen co-founded [NVIDIA](https://aimagazine.com/company/nvidia) in 1993 and has led it through multiple platform shifts, from graphics acceleration to high performance computing and now AI-first infrastructure.
In NVIDIA’s early years, the company came close to collapse after several unsuccessful product launches – an experience he has since cited as formative in shaping his disciplined approach to execution and long-term risk.
That resilience, combined with deep technical fluency, has allowed him to lead NVIDIA through repeated reinvention while maintaining clear direction as the company evolved into an AI-first business.
What separates Jensen from many technology CEOs is continuity.
He has spent decades building both the hardware roadmap and the software ecosystem required to make accelerated computing useful at scale.
That long view also shows in how he describes AI’s impact on the industry.
At the recent CES 2026 in Las Vegas, he argued that “the computer industry is being reinvented”, linking the AI boom to a broader modernisation cycle across computing.
NVIDIA at CES 2026: Automotive Announcements Shaping the Future of Mobility - YouTube
Tap to unmute
![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/qu_6NbSM4o4/hqdefault.jpg)
## Flying the flag for innovation
At CES, Jensen used his keynote stage to [outline NVIDIA’s next AI moves](https://aimagazine.com/news/inside-jensen-huangs-next-ai-moves-as-nvidia-ceo), stressing that the company’s new processors are already in “full production”.
He also claimed the new generation delivers “five times the artificial intelligence computing” of the last generation when used for chatbots and other AI tools.
A central pillar of that roadmap is the Rubin platform, designed to scale from individual servers into larger configurations.
Jensen explained: "This is how we were able to deliver such a gigantic step up in performance, even though we have 1.6 times the number of transistors."
He also focused heavily on inference – the real-time side of AI – where competition is intensifying.
NVIDIA’s answer includes “context memory storage”, aimed at sustaining coherence over longer interactions and more complex prompts.
This matters because influence in AI is increasingly defined not just by training ever-larger models, but by running them efficiently and reliably at scale.
Jensen’s leadership also shows in NVIDIA’s push beyond processors towards autonomous systems.
Introducing Alpamayo, an AI model built for autonomous vehicles, he said: "Not only do we open-source the models, we also open-source the data that we use to train those models, because only in that way can you truly trust how the models came to be.”
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/3656e7bb0995cbb9bd421096cadc49da:82248e7a23661d3d7e55b2d660cc4e38/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-dgx-spark.jpg)
Jenson Huang has led NVIDIA since 1993 (Credit: Nvidia)
## Prioritising AI
When Jensen speaks, audiences listen.
Taking to the stage of at the [World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting 2026 in Davos](https://aimagazine.com/news/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-wef-davos-2026), he positioned AI as a national priority.
"AI is infrastructure and there’s not one country in the world I can’t imagine that you need to have AI as part of your infrastructure," Jensen asserted.
“Because every country has its electricity, you have your roads – you should have AI as part of your infrastructure.”
Ultimately, Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA has defined how AI hardware scales, how infrastructure is conceived and how the technology is being prioritised on a national and global level.
Over the coming years, his influence and decision-making will continue to define the direction of artificial intelligence.
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/c1116d936329170a65e9b5501005c9e5:111f6328a4186565d9ee013b088e0895/ai-top-100-leaders-out-now-cms.jpg)
The Top 100 AI Leaders 2026 is out now
## The Top 100 AI Leaders 2026
The Top 100 AI Leaders 2026 recognises the individuals driving real-world impact through artificial intelligence, from scaling enterprise adoption to advancing responsible and ethical AI.
Our inaugural leaders list highlights the experts and executives who are shaping how AI is developed, governed and deployed across industries including technology, finance, healthcare, manufacturing and energy.
_**To read the Top 100 list in full, [click here](https://aimagazine.com/magazine/top-100-ai-leaders-2026).**_

# KPMG & Uniphore: Embedding AI Agents in Enterprise Workflows
By [Tom Chapman](https://aimagazine.com/author/tom-chapman)
January 27, 2026
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/567947c06f09c0c1529767d294b29c38:4151d394936b70903dff5bc243bfc492/umesh-sachdev-ceo-and-co-founder-of-uniphore.webp)
Umesh Sachdev, CEO and Co-Founder of Uniphore
By integrating Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud into its consulting models, KPMG is moving from isolated AI experiments to deployable, scalable agentic AI
[KPMG](https://aimagazine.com/company/kpmg) has joined forces with Uniphore to operationalise AI agents across enterprise systems, embedding automation within procurement, finance and other business processes.
By integrating Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud into its consulting models, KPMG is moving from isolated AI experiments to deployable, scalable agentic AI systems across multiple sectors.
![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/sCpJIKWI_0s/hqdefault.jpg)
## Building AI agents into the enterprise
Uniphore, a Business AI company, works with data, language models and enterprise systems to create scalable, secure agentic AI. Its aim is to blend the personalised simplicity of consumer AI with the robust scale and governance of enterprise-grade systems.
Global enterprises, including multiple [Fortune 500 companies](https://aimagazine.com/news/the-story-of-metas-agi-team-its-impact-on-the-ai-industry), use Uniphore to update their operations and connect AI with human workflow.
KPMG, one of the largest professional services networks globally, is harnessing the partnership to deploy functional AI agents, enabling automation in procurement, insurance, healthcare and energy workflows.
The collaboration relies on Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud and small language models (SLMs), which are compact, domain-specific versions of large language models. These models are tailored to specific industries or functions, improving performance and alignment with business needs.
The AI agents integrate directly with KPMG’s existing enterprise systems and data environments, enabling reuse of current data architectures while embedding new AI capabilities.
"We are thrilled to align with Uniphore’s vision for AI as a transformative force for business as we focus on helping clients move from AI experimentation to real operational value," says Prasad Jayaraman, Advisory Principal at KPMG.
"Working together with [Uniphore](https://aimagazine.com/company/uniphore) to use AI to transform regulated industries supports our mission to embed business AI into how work gets done, in a way that is governed, scalable and aligned with client needs."
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/e402eefa6eeb70d0f7273cab764ed7b8:5100aa1f95c7fc024647375a71320f56/prasad-jayaraman-advisory-principal-at-kpmg.jpg)
Prasad Jayaraman, Advisory Principal at KPMG
The approach enables KPMG to support clients by building AI-enabled delivery models, covering routine processes through a mix of consulting and AI expertise.
## Meeting sector needs with AI at scale
The partnership introduces a repeatable model to apply AI in highly-regulated and interconnected industries. KPMG is building an AI agent framework that allows its workforce to design, deploy and govern models that blend human input with machine execution.
Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud will help the firm:
- Translate compliance frameworks and institutional knowledge into sector-specific SLMs, so that AI agents can function accurately within regulated boundaries
- Apply governed AI agents across various functions including procurement, finance, workforce optimisation, claims management and customer service
- Extend support to use cases in sectors such as telecommunications, [healthcare](https://aimagazine.com/top10/top-10-ai-platforms-in-healthcare), oil and gas and financial services
This system uses an "SLM factory" approach, where traditional knowledge – once shared through documents and human training – is transformed into reusable and scalable AI tools.
"Business AI proves its value in production, where enterprise environments are complex, regulated and deeply interconnected," adds Umesh Sachdev, CEO and Co-Founder of Uniphore.
"Our work with KPMG enables a repeatable process for running AI inside real enterprise workflows, so organisations can scale how people and AI work together and drive outcomes."
![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/fCwpHFmNNi0/hqdefault.jpg)
Through this process, the AI agents function as operational tools that help enterprises automate, optimise and refine their workflows without disrupting existing systems or governance structures.
## Boosting procurement efficiency
The process targets key pain points for [procurement teams](https://aimagazine.com/news/what-do-governments-risk-without-smarter-ai-procurement), who often face long review cycles and time-consuming risk checks. # KPMG & Uniphore: Embedding AI Agents in Enterprise Workflows
By [Tom Chapman](https://aimagazine.com/author/tom-chapman)
January 27, 2026
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/567947c06f09c0c1529767d294b29c38:4151d394936b70903dff5bc243bfc492/umesh-sachdev-ceo-and-co-founder-of-uniphore.webp)
Umesh Sachdev, CEO and Co-Founder of Uniphore
By integrating Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud into its consulting models, KPMG is moving from isolated AI experiments to deployable, scalable agentic AI
[KPMG](https://aimagazine.com/company/kpmg) has joined forces with Uniphore to operationalise AI agents across enterprise systems, embedding automation within procurement, finance and other business processes.
By integrating Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud into its consulting models, KPMG is moving from isolated AI experiments to deployable, scalable agentic AI systems across multiple sectors.
![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/sCpJIKWI_0s/hqdefault.jpg)
## Building AI agents into the enterprise
Uniphore, a Business AI company, works with data, language models and enterprise systems to create scalable, secure agentic AI. Its aim is to blend the personalised simplicity of consumer AI with the robust scale and governance of enterprise-grade systems.
Global enterprises, including multiple [Fortune 500 companies](https://aimagazine.com/news/the-story-of-metas-agi-team-its-impact-on-the-ai-industry), use Uniphore to update their operations and connect AI with human workflow.
KPMG, one of the largest professional services networks globally, is harnessing the partnership to deploy functional AI agents, enabling automation in procurement, insurance, healthcare and energy workflows.
The collaboration relies on Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud and small language models (SLMs), which are compact, domain-specific versions of large language models. These models are tailored to specific industries or functions, improving performance and alignment with business needs.
The AI agents integrate directly with KPMG’s existing enterprise systems and data environments, enabling reuse of current data architectures while embedding new AI capabilities.
"We are thrilled to align with Uniphore’s vision for AI as a transformative force for business as we focus on helping clients move from AI experimentation to real operational value," says Prasad Jayaraman, Advisory Principal at KPMG.
"Working together with [Uniphore](https://aimagazine.com/company/uniphore) to use AI to transform regulated industries supports our mission to embed business AI into how work gets done, in a way that is governed, scalable and aligned with client needs.”
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/e402eefa6eeb70d0f7273cab764ed7b8:5100aa1f95c7fc024647375a71320f56/prasad-jayaraman-advisory-principal-at-kpmg.jpg)
Prasad Jayaraman, Advisory Principal at KPMG
The approach enables KPMG to support clients by building AI-enabled delivery models, covering routine processes through a mix of consulting and AI expertise.
## Meeting sector needs with AI at scale
The partnership introduces a repeatable model to apply AI in highly-regulated and interconnected industries. KPMG is building an AI agent framework that allows its workforce to design, deploy and govern models that blend human input with machine execution.
Uniphore’s Business AI Cloud will help the firm:
- Translate compliance frameworks and institutional knowledge into sector-specific SLMs, so that AI agents can function accurately within regulated boundaries
- Apply governed AI agents across various functions including procurement, finance, workforce optimisation, claims management and customer service
- Extend support to use cases in sectors such as telecommunications, [healthcare](https://aimagazine.com/top10/top-10-ai-platforms-in-healthcare), oil and gas and financial services
This system uses an "SLM factory" approach, where traditional knowledge – once shared through documents and human training – is transformed into reusable and scalable AI tools.
"Business AI proves its value in production, where enterprise environments are complex, regulated and deeply interconnected," adds Umesh Sachdev, CEO and Co-Founder of Uniphore.
"Our work with KPMG enables a repeatable process for running AI inside real enterprise workflows, so organisations can scale how people and AI work together and drive outcomes."
![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/fCwpHFmNNi0/hqdefault.jpg)
Through this process, the AI agents function as operational tools that help enterprises automate, optimise and refine their workflows without disrupting existing systems or governance structures.
## Boosting procurement efficiency
The process targets key pain points for [procurement teams](https://aimagazine.com/news/what-do-governments-risk-without-smarter-ai-procurement), who often face long review cycles and time-consuming risk checks. AI agents automate those tasks, enabling teams to focus on strategic activities. The model supports both efficiency and accuracy, reducing the likelihood of revenue leakage and compliance oversights.
KPMG and Uniphore are deploying these solutions in environments with fragmented data and strict regulatory frameworks. The goal is to enable AI agents to function effectively – even in settings with multiple dependencies and inconsistent data structures.
Prasad continues: “Uniphore is becoming an increasingly significant player in enterprise AI and we are pleased to work together to help translate business knowledge into AI-enabled delivery models that drive real outcomes for our clients.”
The AI systems are built to operate alongside existing enterprise data platforms. Rather than working in isolation, agents use live data governed by existing controls, allowing businesses to maintain trust in their data while adopting advanced automation.
